items.title: Banach-space Volterra and Dyson series with a norm remainder
items.design_state: A-page mathematical helper: the shared Banach/trace-norm/Dyson existence and remainder result used by the normal, finite-matrix, and algebraic response consumers.
items.statement:
Let $X$ be a complex Banach space, let $T>0$, and let $\mathcal B(X)$ be the bounded complex-linear operators on $X$ with the operator norm. Let $K:[0,T]\to\mathcal B(X)$ be strongly continuous, meaning $t\mapsto K(t)x$ is norm-continuous for every fixed $x\in X$. Suppose a continuous function $a:[0,T]\to[0,\infty)$ satisfies $\|K(t)\|\le a(t)$. Set $c_T=\int_0^T a(s)\,ds$, where the scalar integral is the Riemann integral. Define $\Delta_0(t)=x_0$ and recursively $\Delta_n(t)=\int_0^t K(s)\Delta_{n-1}(s)\,ds$ for $n\ge1$, using the norm-Riemann integral in $X$.

For each $\epsilon\in\mathbb C$, the series $x_\epsilon(t)=\sum_{n=0}^\infty\epsilon^n\Delta_n(t)$ converges uniformly on $[0,T]$. It is the unique continuously differentiable solution of $x_\epsilon'(t)=\epsilon K(t)x_\epsilon(t)$ and $x_\epsilon(0)=x_0$, and

$$\left\|x_\epsilon(t)-x_0-\epsilon\int_0^tK(s)x_0\,ds\right\|\le \|x_0\|\frac{(|\epsilon|c_T)^2e^{|\epsilon|c_T}}{2}.$$

If $X$ is a unital complex $C^*$-algebra and $K(t)x=b(t)x$ for a norm-continuous curve $b:[0,T]\to X$ of skew-adjoint elements, then for real $\epsilon$ the solution with $x_0=1$ is unitary. If $X=\mathcal H$ is a complex Hilbert space and each $K(t)$ is a bounded skew-adjoint operator, then for real $\epsilon$ the solution operators $W_\epsilon(t):x_0\mapsto x_\epsilon(t)$ are unitary even when $K(t)$ is only strongly continuous.

items.title: Finite matrix trace-norm ideal inequalities
items.design_state: A-page mathematical helper: finite trace-norm ideal and trace bounds used by the exact finite-time matrix response.
items.statement:
Let $\mathcal H$ be a complex Hilbert space of finite dimension $d\ge1$. For a matrix $X$ define $|X|=(X^*X)^{1/2}$ by finite Hermitian functional calculus and define its trace norm by $\|X\|_1=\operatorname{Tr}|X|$. This is a complete norm on the finite-dimensional matrix space. For all matrices $X,Y$,
$$
\|YX\|_1\le\|Y\|\|X\|_1,\qquad \|XY\|_1\le\|Y\|\|X\|_1,\qquad |\operatorname{Tr}X|\le\|X\|_1.
$$
For unitary $U$, $\|UXU^*\|_1=\|X\|_1$.

items.title: Lorentzian kernels converge to delta and principal-value distributions
items.design_state: New A-page intermediate result: the test-function proof of the Lorentzian delta and principal-value limits required by the spectral fluctuation–response theorem.
items.statement:
Let $\psi:\mathbb R\to\mathbb C$ be continuously differentiable with compact support. For $\eta>0$, define $P_\eta(x)=\eta/(x^2+\eta^2)$ and $Q_\eta(x)=x/(x^2+\eta^2)$. Define
$$\operatorname{PV}\!\int_{\mathbb R}\frac{\psi(x)}x\,dx:=\lim_{\delta\downarrow0}\int_{|x|>\delta}\frac{\psi(x)}x\,dx$$
when this symmetric limit exists. Then
$$\lim_{\eta\downarrow0}\int_{\mathbb R}P_\eta(x)\psi(x)\,dx=\pi\psi(0),\qquad\lim_{\eta\downarrow0}\int_{\mathbb R}Q_\eta(x)\psi(x)\,dx=\operatorname{PV}\!\int_{\mathbb R}\frac{\psi(x)}x\,dx.$$
Thus $P_\eta$ converges distributionally to $\pi\delta_0$, and $Q_\eta$ converges distributionally to the Cauchy principal-value distribution $\operatorname{PV}(1/x)$, with the stated test-function convention.

items.title: Stationary-state covariance identity for time-integrated observables
items.design_state: New A-page intermediate result: the stationary C*-state double-integral identity and positive covariance matrix required by the Green–Kubo limit.
items.statement:
Let $\mathcal A$ be a unital complex C$^*$-algebra, let $t\mapsto\alpha_t$ be a norm-continuous one-parameter group of $*$-automorphisms, and let $\phi:\mathcal A\to\mathbb C$ be a bounded linear functional with $\phi(I)=1$, $\phi(X^*X)\ge0$ for every $X\in\mathcal A$, and $\phi\circ\alpha_t=\phi$ for every $t$. For $m\ge1$, take self-adjoint $V_1,\ldots,V_m\in\mathcal A$ with $\phi(V_a)=0$. For $T>0$, define the norm-Riemann integrals
$$X_{a,T}=\int_0^T\alpha_t(V_a)\,dt,$$
and for $s\ge0$ define
$$G_{ab}(s)=\frac12\left(\operatorname{Re}\phi(V_a\alpha_s(V_b))+\operatorname{Re}\phi(V_b\alpha_s(V_a))\right).$$
Then each $X_{a,T}$ is self-adjoint and
$$\frac{1}{2T}\operatorname{Re}\phi(X_{a,T}X_{b,T})=\int_0^T\left(1-\frac{s}{T}\right)G_{ab}(s)\,ds.$$
The real symmetric matrix with entries on the left is positive semidefinite.

items.title: Trace-class bounded-observable response
items.design_state: Reserved A-page item; complete local argument follows equilibrium-response.md#T4 with the current inspected supplier interface.
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\mathcal H\ne\{0\}$ be a separable complex Hilbert space, let $H=H^*$ be a densely defined operator with domain $D(H)$, and let $\hbar>0$. Put $U_0(t)=e^{-itH/\hbar}$. Let $\rho$ be a density operator, meaning a positive trace-class operator with $\operatorname{Tr}\rho=1$ as in [[def-qsm-density-trace-state]], and assume $\rho U_0(t)=U_0(t)\rho$ for every $t\in\mathbb R$. Let $A,B\in\mathcal B(\mathcal H)$ be bounded self-adjoint operators, let $T>0$ be a finite time in s, let $h:[0,T]\to\mathbb R$ be continuous, and let $\epsilon\in\mathbb R$ be dimensionless. Interpret $H$ in J, $\hbar$ in J s, and $h(t)B$ in J; if $A,B$ carry units $[A],[B]$, then $R_{AB}$ has units $[A][B]/(\mathrm J\,\mathrm s)$.

Define $B_s=U_0(s)^*BU_0(s)$, $\alpha_t(A)=U_0(t)^*AU_0(t)$, and
$$
R_{AB}(u)=\frac{i}{\hbar}\operatorname{Tr}\!\left(\rho[\alpha_u(A),B]\right),\qquad C_T=\frac2{\hbar}\int_0^T|h(s)|\,\|B\|\,ds.
$$
The trace-class interaction-picture solution of $\rho_I'(t)=\frac{i\epsilon h(t)}{\hbar}[B_t,\rho_I(t)]$, $\rho_I(0)=\rho$, satisfies
$$
\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_I(t)\alpha_t(A))=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho\alpha_t(A))+\epsilon\int_0^t h(s)R_{AB}(t-s)\,ds+r_\epsilon(t),
$$
where $|r_\epsilon(t)|\le\|A\|(|\epsilon|C_T)^2e^{|\epsilon|C_T}/2$ for $0\le t\le T$. Thus the bounded-observable first variation is exact, with an explicit finite-time remainder. No energy or entropy moment of $\rho$ is assumed, and no trace of an unbounded product such as $\rho H A$ is used.

items.title: Finite unitary dynamics and stationary Gibbs states
items.design_state: Reserved A-page item; complete local argument follows equilibrium-response.md#T0 with the current inspected supplier interface.
items.statement:
Let $\mathcal H$ be a complex Hilbert space of finite dimension $d\ge1$, let $H=H^*$ be a Hamiltonian with energy unit J, and let $\hbar>0$ have unit J s. A **finite density matrix** is a positive semidefinite matrix $\rho$ with $\operatorname{Tr}\rho=1$. For time $t\in\mathbb R$ measured in s, set $U(t)=e^{-itH/\hbar}$ and $\alpha_t(A)=U(t)^*AU(t)$. Then $U(t)$ is a unitary group, $\alpha_t$ is a group of matrix $*$-automorphisms, and for every finite density matrix $\rho$ and matrix $A$,

$$\operatorname{Tr}(U(t)\rho U(t)^*A)=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho\alpha_t(A)).$$

The von Neumann entropy $S(\rho)=-k_B\operatorname{Tr}(\rho\log\rho)$ is finite and unchanged by $U(t)\rho U(t)^*$. For $\beta>0$ with unit J$^{-1}$, let $Z_\beta=\operatorname{Tr}(e^{-\beta H})$ and $\sigma_\beta=Z_\beta^{-1}e^{-\beta H}$. Then $Z_\beta>0$, $\sigma_\beta$ is stationary, and the finite Gibbs correlation has the KMS strip identity

$$F_{A,B}(t+i\beta\hbar)=\operatorname{Tr}(\sigma_\beta\alpha_t(B)A),\qquad F_{A,B}(z)=\operatorname{Tr}(\sigma_\beta A\alpha_z(B)),$$

where $\alpha_z(B)=e^{izH/\hbar}Be^{-izH/\hbar}$. The function $F_{A,B}$ is entire and bounded on $0\le\operatorname{Im}z\le\beta\hbar$. This finite-dimensional result asserts no approach to equilibrium.

references.title: Ryogo Kubo, Statistical-Mechanical Theory of Irreversible Processes I, Journal of the Physical Society of Japan 12 (1957), §§2–3

items.title: Finite Cesaro dephasing with degenerate energy blocks
items.design_state: Reserved A-page item; complete local argument follows equilibrium-response.md#T0 with the current inspected supplier interface.
items.statement:
Under the finite-dimensional unitary dynamics of [[thm-qsm-dt-finite-unitary]], let $P_E$ be the orthogonal spectral projection of $H$ for its distinct energy $E$. For every density matrix $\rho$,

$$\frac1T\int_0^T U(t)\rho U(t)^*\,dt\longrightarrow\sum_E P_E\rho P_E$$

in trace norm as $T\to\infty$. The diagonal energy blocks, including all blocks within degenerate eigenspaces, remain. This is Cesaro convergence of the averaged state; pointwise convergence of $U(t)\rho U(t)^*$ is not asserted.

items.title: Finite-time Kubo formula with norm remainder
items.design_state: Reserved A-page item; complete local argument follows equilibrium-response.md#T1 with the current inspected supplier interface.
items.statement:
Let $\mathcal H$ be a complex Hilbert space of finite dimension $d\ge1$, $H=H^*$ with energy unit J, $\hbar>0$ with unit J s, $\beta>0$ with unit J$^{-1}$, and let $\sigma=Z_\beta^{-1}e^{-\beta H}$ be the stationary Gibbs density from [[thm-qsm-dt-finite-unitary]]. Let $A=A^*$ and $B=B^*$ be matrices, let $T>0$ be finite in s, let $h:[0,T]\to\mathbb R$ be continuous, and let $\epsilon\in\mathbb R$ be dimensionless; $h(t)B$ has unit J. Put $U_0(t)=e^{-itH/\hbar}$ for time $t$ in s, $\alpha_t(A)=U_0(t)^*AU_0(t)$, and $B_t=\alpha_t(B)$. Let $W_\epsilon$ solve
$$W_\epsilon'(t)=\frac{i\epsilon h(t)}{\hbar}B_tW_\epsilon(t),\qquad W_\epsilon(0)=I,$$
and set $U_\epsilon(t)=U_0(t)W_\epsilon(t)$ and $\rho_I(t)=W_\epsilon(t)\sigma W_\epsilon(t)^*$. Then $U_\epsilon$ solves $i\hbar U_\epsilon'(t)=(H-\epsilon h(t)B)U_\epsilon(t)$, $U_\epsilon(0)=I$, and $\rho_\epsilon(t):=U_\epsilon(t)\sigma U_\epsilon(t)^*$ satisfies $\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_\epsilon(t)A)=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_I(t)\alpha_t(A))$. Define
$$R_{AB}(u)=\frac{i}{\hbar}\operatorname{Tr}\!\left(\sigma[\alpha_u(A),B]\right),\qquad C_T=\frac{2}{\hbar}\int_0^T|h(s)|\,\|B\|\,ds.$$
Then $W_\epsilon(t)$ is unitary and, for $0\le t\le T$,
$$\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_I(t)\alpha_t(A))=\operatorname{Tr}(\sigma\alpha_t(A))+\epsilon\int_0^t h(s)R_{AB}(t-s)\,ds+r_\epsilon(t),\qquad |r_\epsilon(t)|\le\|A\|\frac{(|\epsilon|C_T)^2e^{|\epsilon|C_T}}2.$$
The initial Gibbs matrix is fixed as $\epsilon$ varies. The result is an exact finite-time first variation with a controlled remainder, not a static derivative of a re-prepared Gibbs family. $C_T$ and $\epsilon$ are dimensionless, and $R_{AB}$ has units $[A][B]/(\mathrm J\,\mathrm s)$.

items.title: Arbitrarily late finite phase recurrences
items.design_state: Reserved A-page item; complete local argument follows equilibrium-response.md#T0 with the current inspected supplier interface.
items.statement: Let $H=H^*$ with energy unit J act on a finite-dimensional complex Hilbert space, let $\hbar>0$ have unit J s, and let $U(t)=e^{-itH/\hbar}$ for time $t$ measured in s. For every time unit $t_0>0$ measured in s, there is a sequence $t_n\to+\infty$ and phases $\lambda_n\in\mathbb C$, $|\lambda_n|=1$, such that $\|U(t_n)-\lambda_n I\|\to0$. Consequently, for every density matrix $\rho$ and bounded observable $A$, the expectation $\operatorname{Tr}(U(t_n)\rho U(t_n)^*A)$ tends to $\operatorname{Tr}(\rho A)$. If $H$ has only one distinct energy, exact recurrences occur at every time.

items.title: Bounded-commutator graph-domain Schrödinger response
items.design_state: Reserved A-page item; complete local argument follows equilibrium-response.md#T4 with the current inspected supplier interface.
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\mathcal H\ne\{0\}$ be separable, $H=H^*$ a densely defined Hamiltonian on $D(H)$ with unit J, $\hbar>0$ with unit J s, $\rho$ a positive trace-class density with $\operatorname{Tr}\rho=1$ and $\rho U_0(t)=U_0(t)\rho$, and $A=A^*\in\mathcal B(\mathcal H)$. Let $B=B^*\in\mathcal B(\mathcal H)$ with unit $[B]$. Assume $B(D(H))\subseteq D(H)$ and that $[H,B]\psi=HB\psi-BH\psi$ on $D(H)$ extends to a bounded operator $C$ on $\mathcal H$. Let $h:[0,T]\to\mathbb R$ be continuous for finite $T>0$ with $h(t)B$ in J, and let $\epsilon\in\mathbb R$ be dimensionless. Then the bounded-observable response and remainder from [[thm-qsm-dt-normal-state-kubo]] hold. In addition, with $U_0(t)=e^{-itH/\hbar}$, $B_t=U_0(t)^*BU_0(t)$, and $W_\epsilon'(t)=i\epsilon h(t)B_tW_\epsilon(t)/\hbar$, $W_\epsilon(0)=I$, the interaction-picture propagator maps $D(H)$ onto itself, and
$$\Psi(t)=U_0(t)W_\epsilon(t)\psi$$
is a strong solution in $\mathcal H$ of $i\hbar\Psi'(t)=(H-\epsilon h(t)B)\Psi(t)$ for each $\psi\in D(H)$. No domain-preservation claim is made for a general bounded $B$ without the stated commutator hypothesis.

items.title: Adopted isolated prepared unitary model
items.design_state: Reserved A-page item; complete local argument follows equilibrium-response.md#T0 with the current inspected supplier interface.
items.statement:
For a specified finite-dimensional complex Hilbert space $\mathcal H$, $H=H^*$ in J, and adopted $\hbar>0$ in J s, take a prepared finite density matrix $\rho_0$ (positive semidefinite with trace one). For time $t$ measured in s, adopt isolated evolution
$$U(t)=e^{-itH/\hbar},\qquad \rho_t=U(t)\rho_0U(t)^*,$$
and the Born expectation $\mathbb E_t[A]=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_tA)$ for each bounded self-adjoint matrix observable $A$. This adopts the finite subsystem's preparation and unitary time evolution as a model assumption. It inherits the full Axiom of Choice convention, stated in [[def-axiom-of-choice]], of [[post-qsm-normal-measurement-state]] for the wider Hilbert-space spectral-measure framework, although this finite bounded-observable clause uses no unbounded spectral measurement. No actual apparatus, measured value, thermalization, or infinite-volume Hamiltonian is asserted.

The finite unitary and Gibbs conventions are stated in [[thm-qsm-dt-finite-unitary]] as formulation context; they do not prove that this postulate describes nature.

items.title: Prepared control and expectation convention
items.design_state: Reserved A-page item; complete local argument follows equilibrium-response.md#T1 with the current inspected supplier interface.
items.statement:
On a finite-dimensional subsystem with unperturbed $H=H^*$ in J, bounded self-adjoint control observable $B$, $\hbar>0$ in J s, and finite interval $[0,T]$ with $T>0$ in s, adopt the idealized controlled Hamiltonian
$$H_\epsilon(t)=H-\epsilon h(t)B,$$
where $h:[0,T]\to\mathbb R$ is continuous, $\epsilon\in\mathbb R$ is dimensionless, and $h(t)B$ has unit J. The initial prepared state is held fixed at $t=0$ as the Gibbs matrix $\sigma=Z_\beta^{-1}e^{-\beta H}$, $\beta>0$ in J$^{-1}$; the model does not re-prepare a Gibbs state for $H_\epsilon(t)$. Expectations use the adopted normal-state Born convention of [[post-qsm-normal-measurement-state]]. The full Axiom of Choice convention, stated in [[def-axiom-of-choice]], of that wider measurement framework is retained. This is an adopted control model; it makes no claim about a particular device or data.

For the controlled propagator $U_\epsilon$ satisfying $i\hbar U_\epsilon'(t)=H_\epsilon(t)U_\epsilon(t)$ and $U_\epsilon(0)=I$, define $\rho_\epsilon(t)=U_\epsilon(t)\sigma U_\epsilon(t)^*$ and $\mathbb E_{\epsilon,t}[A]=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_\epsilon(t)A)$ for bounded self-adjoint matrices $A$. Existence and uniqueness of this finite-dimensional propagator are supplied by [[thm-qsm-dt-finite-kubo]].

The finite-time response theorem [[thm-qsm-dt-finite-kubo]] supplies the exact mathematical response interface used to formulate this postulate. It does not establish the physical applicability of the control model.

items.title: Finite spectral balance and distributional fluctuation response
items.design_state: Reserved A-page item; complete local argument follows equilibrium-response.md#T2 with the current inspected supplier interface.
items.statement:
Let $\mathcal H$ be finite-dimensional, $H=H^*$ with unit J, $\hbar>0$ with unit J s, $\beta>0$ with unit J$^{-1}$, and $\sigma=Z_\beta^{-1}e^{-\beta H}$ as in [[thm-qsm-dt-finite-unitary]]. Let $A=A^*$ be a matrix observable, write $Hu_i=E_i u_i$ in an orthonormal eigenbasis, $r_i=e^{-\beta E_i}/Z_\beta$, $A_{ij}=\langle Au_j,u_i\rangle$, and $\omega_{ji}=(E_j-E_i)/\hbar$. Define the finite positive spectral measure
$$S_{AA}=2\pi\sum_{i,j}r_i|A_{ij}|^2\,\delta_{\omega_{ji}},$$
where $\delta_\nu$ is unit point mass at frequency $\nu$ and $S_{AA}(-\cdot)$ denotes pushforward under $\omega\mapsto-\omega$; $\omega_{ji}$ has unit s$^{-1}$. With observable unit $[A]$, $S_{AA}$ has unit $[A]^2\,\mathrm s$. The equilibrium correlation is $C_{AA}(t)=\operatorname{Tr}(\sigma\alpha_t(A)A)$, and its Fourier convention is $S_{AA}(\omega)=\int_{\mathbb R}e^{i\omega t}C_{AA}(t)\,dt$ in the distributional sense.

For $t\ge0$, set $R_{AA}(t)=\frac{i}{\hbar}\operatorname{Tr}(\sigma[\alpha_t(A),A])$ and, for $\eta>0$, define the retarded transform $\chi_\eta(\omega)=\int_0^\infty e^{(i\omega-\eta)t}R_{AA}(t)\,dt$. Then
$$\chi_\eta(\omega)=\sum_{i,j}\frac{(r_i-r_j)|A_{ij}|^2}{\hbar(\omega_{ji}-\omega-i\eta)}.$$
As $\eta\downarrow0$, its boundary value is the corresponding sum of principal-value real parts and Lorentzian imaginary terms weighted by $r_i-r_j$, and distributionally
$$\operatorname{Im}\chi=\frac{1}{2\hbar}(1-e^{-\beta\hbar\omega})S_{AA}(\omega).$$
Detailed balance is $S_{AA}(-d\omega)=e^{-\beta\hbar\omega}S_{AA}(d\omega)$. Thus, on $\mathbb R\setminus\{0\}$,
$$S_{\mathrm{sym}}(d\omega)=\hbar\coth\!\left(\frac{\beta\hbar\omega}{2}\right)\operatorname{Im}\chi(d\omega),\qquad S_{\mathrm{sym}}=\tfrac12(S_{AA}+S_{AA}(-\cdot)).$$
Any zero-frequency mass of $S_{AA}$ is retained separately: the commutator factor vanishes there, so the formula does not determine that atom or define a value for the singular product with $\coth$ at $\omega=0$.

items.title: Absolute convergence of trace-Gibbs bounded correlation series
items.design_state: New A-page intermediate result: the absolute double-series estimate and finite spectral measure needed for trace-Gibbs detailed balance.
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\mathcal H\ne\{0\}$ be separable, $K=K^*$ a densely defined Hamiltonian bounded below with energy unit J, and $\beta$ lie in an open interval $I\subset(0,\infty)$ measured in J$^{-1}$ on which $e^{-sK}$ is trace class for every $s\in I$. Set $Z_\beta=\operatorname{Tr}(e^{-\beta K})$, $\sigma_\beta=Z_\beta^{-1}e^{-\beta K}$, and $U(t)=e^{-itK/\hbar}$ with $\hbar>0$ in J s and $t$ in s. By [[thm-qsm-trace-gibbs-variational]], $K$ has a complete orthonormal energy basis $(u_i)$, $Ku_i=E_i u_i$, with Gibbs weights $r_i=e^{-\beta E_i}/Z_\beta>0$ and $\sum_i r_i=1$. For bounded $A,B$, put $A_{ij}=\langle Au_j,u_i\rangle$, $B_{ij}=\langle Bu_j,u_i\rangle$, and $\omega_{ji}=(E_j-E_i)/\hbar$. Then
$$C_{AB}(t):=\operatorname{Tr}(\sigma_\beta U(t)^*AU(t)B)=\sum_{i,j}r_iA_{ij}B_{ji}e^{-i\omega_{ji}t}$$
converges absolutely and uniformly on $\mathbb R$, with $\sum_{i,j}r_i|A_{ij}||B_{ji}|\le\|A\|\|B\|$. Consequently
$$S_{AB}:=2\pi\sum_{i,j}r_iA_{ij}B_{ji}\,\delta_{\omega_{ji}}$$
is a finite complex Borel measure with total variation at most $2\pi\|A\|\|B\|$, and $C_{AB}(t)=(2\pi)^{-1}\int e^{-i\omega t}\,dS_{AB}(\omega)$. A Dirac measure $\delta_\nu$ assigns mass one to the point $\nu$. The measure $S_{AB}$ has units $[A][B]$ s when $A,B$ carry units $[A],[B]$.

references.title: Ryogo Kubo, Statistical-Mechanical Theory of Irreversible Processes I, Journal of the Physical Society of Japan 12 (1957), §2, printed pp. 573–575
MIT OpenCourseWare 8.512, Theory of Solids II, Lecture 1: Linear Response Theory, §1.3

items.title: Trace-Gibbs bounded correlation measure and balance
items.design_state: Reserved A-page item; complete local argument follows equilibrium-response.md#T2 with the current inspected supplier interface.
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\mathcal H\ne\{0\}$ be separable, $K=K^*$ densely defined and bounded below with energy unit J, and let $e^{-sK}$ be trace class for every $s$ in an open interval $I\subset(0,\infty)$ measured in J$^{-1}$. Fix $\beta\in I$, $Z_\beta=\operatorname{Tr}(e^{-\beta K})$, $\sigma_\beta=Z_\beta^{-1}e^{-\beta K}$, and $U(t)=e^{-itK/\hbar}$ for $\hbar>0$ in J s and $t$ in s. For bounded $A,B$, let $C_{AB}$ and $S_{AB}$ be the correlation function and finite spectral measure defined in [[lem-qsm-dt-trace-gibbs-correlation-series]]. Write $S_{BA}(-\cdot)$ for the pushforward under $\omega\mapsto-\omega$. Then for every bounded Borel test function $f$ with compact support,
$$\int f(\omega)\,S_{BA}(-d\omega)=\int f(\omega)e^{-\beta\hbar\omega}\,S_{AB}(d\omega).$$
The weighted measure on the right extends to a finite complex measure: the reindexed coefficient family is absolutely summable and has the same total-variation bound as $S_{BA}$. For Hermitian $A=B$, $S_{AA}$ is a positive finite measure. This is a discrete-spectrum equilibrium correlation identity; it asserts no temporal decay, continuum limit, or ordinary zero-frequency transport coefficient.

items.title: Conditional prepared finite quantum control response
items.design_state: Reserved A-page item; complete local argument follows equilibrium-response.md#T1 with the current inspected supplier interface.
items.statement:
Assume the adopted finite isolated model and fixed-preparation control convention of [[post-qsm-dt-isolated-model]] and [[post-qsm-dt-physical-control]]. Let $T>0$ be finite in s, let $A=A^*$ be a bounded matrix observable, and set $\alpha_t(A)=e^{itH/\hbar}Ae^{-itH/\hbar}$ for time $t$ measured in s. Define
$$R_{AB}(u)=\frac{i}{\hbar}\operatorname{Tr}\!\left(\sigma[\alpha_u(A),B]\right),\qquad C_T=\frac2\hbar\int_0^T|h(s)|\,\|B\|\,ds.$$
Then for $0\le t\le T$ the model expectation obeys
$$\mathbb E_{\epsilon,t}[A]=\operatorname{Tr}(\sigma\alpha_t(A))+\epsilon\int_0^t h(s)R_{AB}(t-s)\,ds+r_\epsilon(t),\qquad |r_\epsilon(t)|\le\|A\|\frac{(|\epsilon|C_T)^2e^{|\epsilon|C_T}}2.$$
Here $H$ and $hB$ have unit J, $\hbar$ has unit J s, $t$ has unit s, $\beta$ has unit J$^{-1}$, and $\epsilon,C_T$ are dimensionless. This is a conditional model prediction for the adopted preparation and dynamics, not a claim that an observed finite dataset must equal the prediction.

references.title: Ryogo Kubo, Statistical-Mechanical Theory of Irreversible Processes I, Journal of the Physical Society of Japan 12 (1957), §2, printed pp. 572–575
MIT OpenCourseWare 8.512, Theory of Solids II, Lecture 1: Linear Response Theory, §§1.1–1.2

items.physical_scope: Exact prediction of the specified finite-dimensional isolated-control model under its adopted preparation, unitary-evolution, and Born-expectation postulates; it is not an observation, an apparatus validation, or evidence that the model describes nature.

items.title: Bounded C-star Dyson response for finite-range spin dynamics
items.design_state: Reserved A-page item; complete local argument follows equilibrium-response.md#T3 with the current inspected supplier interface.
items.statement:
Use $\Gamma=\mathbb Z^d$, $d\ge1$, finite on-site dimension $q\ge1$, and a uniformly bounded finite-range interaction $\Phi$ with parameters $M\ge1$, $R<\infty$, $\kappa<\infty$, and $\hbar>0$ as in [[def-qsm-bounded-finite-range-interaction]]. Assume Countable Choice and the exact finite-matrix C$^*$-identity condition supplied in [[lem-qsm-finite-matrix-cstar-and-state-duality]]. Let $\mathcal A$ be the norm-completed quasi-local spin algebra of [[def-qsm-quasilocal-spin-algebra]], and let $\alpha_t$ be the strongly continuous automorphism group of [[thm-qsm-finite-range-spin-dynamics]]. Let $\{\rho_\Lambda\}$ be consistent positive trace-one local density matrices; write $\phi$ for their unique state extension supplied by [[lem-qsm-consistent-local-states]], and additionally assume $\phi\circ\alpha_t=\phi$ for every $t\in\mathbb R$. This is an algebraic state on $\mathcal A$, not a trace-class density on an infinite tensor-product Hilbert space.

For $A\in\mathcal A$, $B=B^*\in\mathcal A$, continuous real $h:[0,T]\to\mathbb R$, finite $T>0$, and dimensionless $\epsilon\in\mathbb R$, put $B_t=\alpha_t(B)$ and let $W_\epsilon$ solve
$$W_\epsilon'(t)=\frac{i\epsilon h(t)}{\hbar}B_tW_\epsilon(t),\qquad W_\epsilon(0)=I.$$
The C$^*$-algebra Dyson solution is unitary. Define $\alpha_t^\epsilon(A)=W_\epsilon(t)^*\alpha_t(A)W_\epsilon(t)$,
$$R_{AB}(u)=\frac{i}{\hbar}\phi([\alpha_u(A),B]),\qquad C_T=\frac2\hbar\int_0^T|h(s)|\,\|B\|\,ds.$$
Then
$$\phi(\alpha_t^\epsilon(A))=\phi(\alpha_t(A))+\epsilon\int_0^t h(s)R_{AB}(t-s)\,ds+r_\epsilon(t),\qquad |r_\epsilon(t)|\le\|A\|\frac{(|\epsilon|C_T)^2e^{|\epsilon|C_T}}2.$$
When energy is the interpretation of $H_\Lambda$ and $hB$, their units are J, $t$ is s, $\hbar$ is J s, and $C_T$ is dimensionless. No global trace Hamiltonian, spatial-to-temporal decay implication, or dc coefficient follows.

references.title: Pieter Naaijkens, Quantum Spin Systems on Infinite Lattices, Theorem 3.3.12 and proof, printed pp. 69–71
MIT OpenCourseWare 8.512, Theory of Solids II, Lecture 1: Linear Response Theory, §§1.1–1.2

items.title: Nonzero pure-point equilibrium covariance is not integrable
items.design_state: Reserved A-page item; complete local argument follows equilibrium-response.md#T5 with the current inspected supplier interface.
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the trace-class Gibbs hypotheses of [[thm-qsm-dt-trace-gibbs-correlation-measure]] for a self-adjoint Hamiltonian $K$ in J with a complete discrete energy basis and faithful Gibbs density $\sigma_\beta$ at $\beta>0$ in J$^{-1}$. Let $\hbar>0$ be in J s, $t$ in s, and let $A=A^*$ be a nonzero bounded observable with $\operatorname{Tr}(\sigma_\beta A)=0$. Define
$$C_{AA}(t)=\operatorname{Tr}(\sigma_\beta U(t)^*AU(t)A),\qquad G_{AA}(t)=\operatorname{Re}C_{AA}(t),\qquad U(t)=e^{-itK/\hbar}.$$
Then neither $C_{AA}$ nor $G_{AA}$ belongs to $L^1([0,\infty))$. In particular, the ordinary absolutely convergent isolated-system correlation integral used in a dc Green–Kubo formula does not exist under these hypotheses. This claim concerns discrete-spectrum trace-Gibbs dynamics only; it asserts no failure of temporal decay or transport limits in an infinite-volume or open-system model.

references.title: Ryogo Kubo, Statistical-Mechanical Theory of Irreversible Processes I, Journal of the Physical Society of Japan 12 (1957), §3, printed p. 575
MIT OpenCourseWare 8.512, Theory of Solids II, Lecture 1: Linear Response Theory, §1.5

items.title: Integrability-qualified quantum variance Green–Kubo limit
items.design_state: Reserved A-page item; complete local argument follows equilibrium-response.md#T5 with the current inspected supplier interface.
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice and the finite-matrix C$^*$-identity hypothesis used by [[thm-qsm-dt-algebraic-kubo]]. Use its finite-range spin algebra $\mathcal A$, strongly continuous automorphism group $\alpha_t$, and invariant state $\phi$ obtained from consistent local densities. Let $V=V^*\in\mathcal A$ satisfy $\phi(V)=0$, and define
$$X_T=\int_0^T\alpha_t(V)\,dt,\qquad G(t)=\operatorname{Re}\phi(V\alpha_t(V)).$$
If $G\in L^1([0,\infty))$, then
$$\lim_{T\to\infty}\frac{\phi(X_T^2)}{2T}=D:=\int_0^\infty G(t)\,dt\ge0.$$
For a finite list of centered self-adjoint observables $V_1,\ldots,V_m$, if each symmetrized covariance $G_{ab}(t)=\tfrac12(\operatorname{Re}\phi(V_a\alpha_t(V_b))+\operatorname{Re}\phi(V_b\alpha_t(V_a)))$ is absolutely integrable on $[0,\infty)$, then $D_{ab}=\int_0^\infty G_{ab}(t)dt$ is a real positive semidefinite matrix. For a velocity observable measured in m s$^{-1}$, $D$ has units m$^2$ s$^{-1}$; for general $V$, its units are $[V]^2$ s. The result is a variance of a time-integrated observable, not a joint classical trajectory or a universal transport law.

references.title: Ryogo Kubo, Statistical-Mechanical Theory of Irreversible Processes I, Journal of the Physical Society of Japan 12 (1957), §§2–3, printed pp. 573–575
Pieter Naaijkens, Quantum Spin Systems on Infinite Lattices, Theorem 3.3.12 and proof, printed pp. 69–71

items.title: Projected oscillator transition response
items.design_state: Reserved B-page item; complete local argument follows equilibrium-response.md#T4 with the current inspected supplier interface.
items.statement:
Let $\mathcal H=\ell^2(\mathbb N_0)$ with standard orthonormal basis $(e_n)_{n\ge0}$. Fix $\omega>0$ in s$^{-1}$ and $\hbar>0$ in J s. Define the diagonal Hamiltonian
$$He_n=\hbar\omega(n+\tfrac12)e_n,\qquad D(H)=\{c\in\ell^2:\sum_{n\ge0}(n+\tfrac12)^2|c_n|^2<\infty\}.$$
For real $b_0\ne0$ in the chosen observable unit, define the bounded transition observable $B=b_0(|e_0\rangle\langle e_1|+|e_1\rangle\langle e_0|)$ and set $A=B$. Let $\beta>0$ in J$^{-1}$, $q=e^{-\beta\hbar\omega}$, and $\Delta=\hbar\omega$. On a finite interval $[0,T]$ with $T>0$ in s, drive with a constant real field $h(t)=h_0$ and dimensionless $\epsilon\in\mathbb R$, where $h_0B$ has unit J. This is a bounded projection between the first two oscillator levels, not the unbounded oscillator position.
